report:
**Conclusion:** 
The health claim is **true**. Contrary to your initial impression, robust clinical trial evidence and regulatory approvals confirm that abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

**Key Evidence:**
* **Clinical Trial Data:** The pivotal Phase 3 ACTIVE trial published in *JAMA* found that 18 months of daily subcutaneous abaloparatide reduced the risk of new morphometric vertebral fractures by **86%** compared to placebo (0.6% vs. 4.2%, $p < 0.001$).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** Comprehensive network meta-analyses and systematic reviews consistently show that abaloparatide provides substantial vertebral fracture reduction and improvements in bone mineral density compared to placebo and alternative osteoporosis therapies.
* **Regulatory Approval:** Based on results from the ACTIVE trial and its extension study, the U.S. FDA approved abaloparatide (brand name Tymlos) in 2017 specifically to reduce the risk of vertebral and nonvertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with high-risk osteoporosis.

**Sources Cited:**
1. JAMA Clinical Trial (Miller et al.): https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640
2. FDA Prescribing Information Label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf
3. Osteoporosis International Network Meta-Analysis: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-019-04947-2
4. MDPI Systematic Review on Abaloparatide: https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/2/673
